Beyond the Glory

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
turning the glory of the game into a greater good for all

Further information:
This is a story about teenagers learning empathy in a world broken by absent adults, greed and ego.
Teenagers standing up and taking action, being taught to use the skills they have to create a better world

Rugby and South Africans are an ancient love story that never gets old. It starts at school, making the first team is a rite of passage praised by parents and teachers, the boys are treated like gods, and every time they go onto that field, they break their bodies for the prestige of the win.

In 2018 Jono Kruger, the head of rugby at Selbourne College, started to wonder if there wasn’t a way to make it all mean more, “How could I get these kids to play for more than the glory, how could we hardness all this commitment to create a positive change in the world”. After a while he decided to launch a campaign at Selbourne called ‘Tries for Lives’. For every try that the 1st team scored that year people could donate money towards an NGO, the boys chose a local safe house woman and children.

Chris Kingsley, the head of house, at Hilton Collage caught onto the idea and started the same initiative at Hilton Collage, “for me I wanted to teach these boys to think beyond themselves, to use their privilege for good”. The boys selected a local children’s home, which they did community work at throughout the year.
At the end of the year, together the schools managed to raise R150k for both homes.

In 2020 Jono and Chris decided to join forces and create Sports for Lives, an online fundraising platform like BackaBuddy etc, which allows young sports players to easily start a campaign and people to donate online.
“We are turning athletes into activists, inspiring them to play for a higher purpose.”
Currently there are over 30 active campaigns from all over South Africa.

In KZN, St Annes 1st team hockey players are raising funds for a GBV women’s shelter, In Cape Town Jaime, a 13-year-old pupil, is swimming for a Rhino conservation project, the netball girls of exclusive private school ST. Cyprians are playing 2022 for the Mitchells Plain netball union “instead of being ashamed of our privilege we want to put it to good use”

There are two current campaigns that I thought we could zone in on:
In East-London a group of Selbourne boys just ran 300k in 6 days, covering 50km/day, for a fellow pupil Ubuko, who lost both his legs and 6 of his fingers to gangrene, caused by meningococcal septicaemia. It is part of a larger campaign to raise 600k to get Ubuko a mechanic hand.
They finished on Wednesday 7th July and documented the whole Journey

In 2021 Simnikiwe Bosman, one of Graeme Collages star rugby players, injured his Knee. The injury resulted in his leg having to be amputated. The 1st team has dedicated every try scored this year to Simnikiwe. There is footage of the accident and of him leading the 1st team in a war cry prior to the game

Script:


BEYOND THE GLORY

Playing first team rugby is a rite of passage for so many school boys across the country.
And when they finally get that first team jersey and run onto the field they will sacrifice anything for the glory of the win

JONO
I have a background in
NGO work
And when I became a teacher, I quickly
found that a lot of the boys play for
for the glory and for the win
And I thought of this idea, what if we could play for something bigger than success?
Could we be doing something bigger than just winning games?


LINK: In 2017 Jono Kruger, a coach and teacher at Selbourne Collage wanted to find a way to harness the passion and commitment of the teenagers he was coaching, and get them to start playing for a higher purpose, one beyond themselves

JONO: Our country is the most unequal country in the world, and our boys didn't know anything about that

Kruger took the first team rugby boys to a local children's home and they committed their season to those children. he then setup an online fundraising platform, tries for lives, where people could donate to every try the team scored
Elite private school Hilton Collage also came on board and within that first year they managed to raise over 150 00 rand by scoring tries.

I don't think we need to be ashamed of our privilege. But I do think that we could do more with our privilege

Tries for lives grew and has become run for lives, swim for lives, goals for lives, and birdies for lives, all these campaigns are being started by teenagers around South Africa trying to change the world


SIM:
rugby was my life.
I'm day at school and after school
you know, and everything revolved around
rugby for me.
When I'm playing a game, it feels like.
no one's around

in 2021 Simnikiwe Bosman’s dream of making the first came true but Halfway through the season Simnikiwe was badly injured, his bestfriend and teammate Hlombe kepe was running behind him when he went down

HLOMBE
we're playing against St Andrews Derby game and Andrews last year
he was saving a try.
that guy just fell on with you.
and then like I just heard him shouting

Simnikiwe never returned to the field, due to the complexity of the injury his right leg had to abe mputated from above the knee.

SIM:
everything changed so quickly.
miss everything about rugby
and being able to be on the field

HLOMBE
he's my best friend.
HE LOST HIS LEG BECAUSE of the sport that I played.
the only way to help him for me is TO play good rugby,

Hlombe and the rest of the first team have dedicated their 2022 season to Simnikiwe, through their sports for lives campaign.

Hlombe
when I play rugby,
I just think of my best friend I play for him

when Ubuko was 2 years old he contracted Meningococcal meningitis, it is a fast-acting disease that resulted in him losing both his legs and 7 of his fingers

UBUKO:
because I always use my one hand and using only one hand, which is half fingers and two full fingers. It's hard because I can grab onto things. but I can't do anything with this hand.
Verite beat of him – we can see what scenes we have


Ubuko is a bursary student at Selborne college, and this year the college are using the Sport for lives platform, across muliple sporting diciuplines, to raise 600 000, so that Ubuko can get a mechanical hand




BRAD
I realised that it would take quite a few years to get to the total target of the money that we require
AND for me, I would like to raise enough money for Kuku to get his hand by the end of the year

As the head boy Bradly smith wanted to do more, so he signed up a few mates and together with kruger they committed to running from Port-elizabeth to East-london covering a distance of 300km over 6 days

GOITSI
when Brad and Mr. Krueger, they were all like, yeah, you should come. You can help out to this massive initiative. I was like, at first I was like, Nah, I got to be crazy because noise. I'm running 300 kilometers.
BUT there was a stage where I saw Mr. Kruger running and he looked up for, maybe I'd say around 30 seconds,
give me time to reflect on myself and also realize that this isn't just for me

The team of 5 ran for 6 gruelling days, they got shin splits, they lost toe nails, every muscle in their bodies seized up, but they woke up every morning at 3am and they ran

BRAD:
we were running between two of our safety vehicles and on the back of our, of the car that was in front of us had a
big banner of a buckle and these prosthetic legs and his two hands there. And that just gave us a constant reminder, really, whenever we looked up

The team completed the Ubuko 300 on the 10 of July and raised over 60 000 rand

GOITSI AND BRAD:
What's the first thing you guys did when you got home after that run?
I realized that actually I wasn't done. What I mean by that was that on day four,
unfortunately, didn't complete the day because my left foot was just too much in pain.
So I decided to create a day seven for myself and literally go back and complete the distance that I didn't.

Bradly got up at 3am on Day 7, and with his father following him as a safety vehicle he walked for 12 hours to complete the 300 km distance that he committed to Ubuko


I realized that.
I'm actually privileged to have pain, I'm privileged to feel pain in my legs because I have legs.

Simnikiwe is in the process of training as a potential paralympic runner for Paris 2024, all the funds that his team are raising, by scoring tries, will go towards his training requirements

SIM: I'm very grateful to them, you know, and
they didn't actually have to do it for me.
I'm just trying to figure out what's next

JONO:
I think we've got to we've got to start as a nation to look beyond the glory of the win
what if schools around the country could actually be the catalyst to social change in our country? Whats happens if community upliftment started at the school level?
Some hero Sim shot in his blade
